how: Help is recruited from neighbouring counties around a flag already appearing on the canvas.
A claimed heart and an emerging county flag establish different reported marks without establishing their visual relationship.
A participant reports that the county flag is appearing and gives its coordinates.
A question about where to put the flag receives coordinates locating a flag that already exists.
Participants question the flag's orange colour, explain a yellow interpretation, and report that correction is underway.
The colour interpretation does not identify who placed or corrected the pixels.
A warning that the flag replaced Cornish work receives an apology for not realising.
An endorsed space-sharing design and a reported alliance show accommodation talk without establishing implementation or bilateral assent.
Reported replacement of Cornish work does not establish the placers, their intent, or an attack call.
The ending inventory reports missing pixels but contains no observed relocation of the county flag.
Learning that the flag already exists receives an immediate celebration.
A final inventory distinguishes the county's missing pixels from neighbouring flags' survival and destruction without identifying causes.
The final inventory supplies no observed proposal to carry the effort into another canvas or lasting collective activity.
The recorded repair exchange does not name scripts, spare accounts, or any other placement automation.
A self-identified neighbour offers help in a joining line, and a later reply explicitly endorses the proposed design.
Participants recruit neighbour help, receive an offer, and later state a reciprocal looking-after rationale.
A participant reports believing in an alliance with both adjacent counties, followed by a wish for more county flags.
The final damage report neither taunts a rival nor claims victory or names an attacker to blame.
Earlier occupation and proposed shared space do not establish a host's authority over guests.
The neighbour recruitment passage does not establish any host-sub rule or decision about containing canvas discussion.
The reported alliance receives a wish for additional county flags rather than an observed challenge to who may bind participants.
Reporting missing pixels and a neighbour's destruction does not establish a dispute about cleanup or which version should be preserved.
The title's claim of stealing a heart does not establish a host-sub takeover, fake, or April Fools framing.
The flag-location question is answered by finding an existing flag without any observed judgement of insufficient hands.
The warning concerns displaced canvas work and supplies no observed quarrel predating the canvas.
County flags and a wish to gather counties do not establish broader history, ideology, lore, or allegiance to a colour.
Informal proposal, endorsement, and alliance passages cannot establish the global frequency claim or the local absence of decided organization.
No cited turn connects an inherited tie to an attack on another room.
Claiming a heart and reporting an emerging flag do not identify a flag originator whom others joined.
A visiting member's offer and warning do not establish that the member carried a proposal between venues.
The flag is already appearing before neighbour recruitment, and the record does not identify construction caused by that recruitment.
The heart claimant and flag reporter cannot be established as the starter whose action caused neighbour recruitment.
The appearing flag precedes colour correction without a passage explaining correction as the consequence of completion or fear of loss.
Use the upkeep-to-negotiation route only where upkeep prompts negotiation, since neighbour accommodation here precedes the recorded colour correction.
The settled-border mechanism does not explain an apology directly answering newly disclosed displacement before the proposed shared layout.
No cited turn tests whether reported correction caused adoption of machine placement.
The coordinate answer directly receives celebration of the existing flag without requiring it to be finished.
Celebration precedes the ending inventory without a passage showing that celebration prompted recording.
The ending inventory provides no subsequent decision through which recording could be shown to cause continuation.
The resolved location question and ending inventory show neither a strength judgement nor a move whose causal connection could be tested.
A design proposal and later coordinates belong to different exchanges and do not establish a pixel template settling design disagreement.
The neighbour-help proposal receives an explicit joining response from a self-identified member of the named neighbour.
Neighbour help precedes the recorded repair and no cited passage explains recruitment through a shortage of hands under strain.
Help is offered before the shared-layout proposal without a passage showing border talk opening the channel for help.
The recruitment and displacement warning do not establish a call turning helpers toward an attack.
The apology answers a displacement warning rather than a documented attack call, leaving the attack-call mechanism untested.
Accommodation follows a displacement warning without establishing an attack call as its cause.
Reported displacement and final destruction do not establish an attack causing a continuing verbal contest.
The repair report and later alliance belief do not establish shared attack or upkeep strain as the reason for joining.
Neighbour recruitment supplies no evidence of a canvas flood producing a host-sub boundary.
The reported alliance receives no recorded challenge to representative authority, leaving the tentative dispute route unobserved.
Treat colour correction as upkeep without assuming hostile erosion when participants report a mistaken colour interpretation rather than an attacker.
Learning that a flag replaced a neighbour's work prompts an apology before any settled border is documented.
A bare joining passage can coexist with a territorial warning in the same turn, so accepting help does not establish unqualified approval of the arrangement.
